nodes.name: Capture Webhook
nodes.notes: POST only, and the path is the workflow id spelled out rather than left to the node id n8n mints, so the production URL is one a client can be configured with before this file has ever reached an instance. Response mode onReceived, so the request is answered as it lands and the pass runs behind it: the alternative holds the socket open through extraction, the findings write and the invocation of ar-score, none of which a capture client asked about. authentication is written none rather than left off, because a default nobody wrote down is a decision nobody reviewed; what stands in front of this path is whatever fronts the instance, and this canvas judges shape rather than caller. typeVersion 2 is what the other nodes here are held to as well: nothing in this repository validates an n8n parameter name or version, no n8n package being installed, so these four are reviewed rather than checked.

parameters.query:
WITH envelope AS (
  SELECT nullif($1::jsonb, 'null'::jsonb) AS posted
),
claim AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN e.posted ->> 'sourceId' ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
      THEN (e.posted ->> 'sourceId')::bigint
    END AS source_id
  FROM envelope e
),
source AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.domain_id,
    s.kind,
    s.endpoint,
    s.parser_config,
    s.contract,
    s.consecutive_failures,
    s.last_success_at,
    s.last_failure_at,
    s.enabled,
    s.flagged
  FROM sources s
  WHERE s.id = (SELECT source_id FROM claim)
)
-- The first node after the trigger, and the shape the parent design fixes for every
-- workflow in this set (.specs/2026-08-19-research-pipeline-port.md, section 4): the
-- domain's personas and taxonomy, read as ONE query answering exactly one row. Both
-- halves are argued in full on ar-ingest's Load Domain Context, which asks the same
-- question of the same tables and is not repeated here. What is written out below is
-- the half that differs, which is how this canvas gets a domain at all.

-- Nothing has named one. ar-ingest is invoked with a run id and reads its domain back
-- off that row, an id the dispatcher wrote. All this trigger carries is a POST body
-- from a stranger, and no part of it has been judged: capture-contract.ts runs two
-- node groups below, after the raw body has been stored. So the domain is resolved
-- through the source the envelope CLAIMS, and this statement is where the claim is
-- read.

-- The whole posted body binds as ONE jsonb parameter rather than one parameter per
-- member. A body may be a bare string, a number or a list as readily as an object,
-- JSON.stringify makes every one of those a valid jsonb literal, and the members are
-- then read where a comment can say what each one is instead of inside an expression
-- no gate reads. The nullif is the other half of that: JSON.stringify(null) binds the
-- JSON null literal rather than SQL NULL, so a request with no body at all would
-- otherwise arrive here as a value.

-- ->> answers NULL for every jsonb that is not an object, measured on this schema for
-- a string, a number, a list and the null literal, so a body that is not an object
-- needs no guard in front of the read: the pattern test is handed NULL, the CASE
-- answers NULL, and nothing raises over a shape somebody else chose.

-- The digit bound is {1,18} rather than +, and the difference between them is a
-- raise. A longer run of digits matches + and then overflows the bigint cast, which
-- is an error this node could not survive; eighteen digits sits inside bigint's
-- nineteen, and no sources id is going to reach it.

-- Three readings come out of this row and they are not two. A null source_id means
-- the envelope named no source this statement could read. A source_id with a null
-- domain_id means it named one that matches no sources row. A domain_id means the
-- capture resolved, and an empty list beside it is a domain that states no personas,
-- no categories, no terms or no criteria. Read them in that order: a length says
-- nothing until both ids have been read.

-- Nothing here refuses, which is the rule capture-contract.ts states from the other
-- side. The raw body is stored before anything judges it, so a node turning an
-- unreadable source id away HERE would lose the capture at exactly the point that
-- ordering exists to protect. What this answers instead is a row saying what it could
-- and could not resolve. One thing the group below cannot do with it is store a
-- document under a null domain: documents.domain_id is NOT NULL, so a capture naming
-- a source this database does not hold has no row to be written to, and what that
-- pass records is that group's to decide.

-- The source row is fetched here rather than by a lookup node below because this is
-- where it is read anyway: the domain is reached THROUGH it, so the round trip is
-- already spent and a second node would be a second branch to reason about. to_jsonb
-- over the CTE is what projects it, so the member list is declared once, in the CTE
-- above, and a column added there travels with no second edit. This node acts on none
-- of them: enabled and flagged are answers rather than decisions here.

-- The posted body is not echoed forward. This node's answer REPLACES the item the
-- trigger was handed, which is what run_id travels for on ar-ingest's twin, but a
-- capture body IS the payload and copying it onto every item below would carry the
-- whole capture through the pass. The node that stores it reads it back off
-- $('Capture Webhook').first().json.body, which is the handle every node here has on
-- the request.

-- Every list is ordered, which nothing downstream requires and every reader benefits
-- from: two captures against one unchanged domain hand the nodes below the same lists
-- in the same order, so a diff between two passes is about the captures rather than
-- about the order a planner happened to return rows in.
SELECT
  (SELECT source_id FROM claim) AS source_id,
  (SELECT domain_id FROM source) AS domain_id,

  -- The source row, cut to the members the groups below read. It is also the
  -- resolution path: domain_id comes off it, so every list beneath is scoped by a
  -- column of this row rather than by anything the envelope said. parser_config and
  -- contract are what the extraction reads, the two stamps and the counter are what
  -- source-health.ts turns into a verdict, and kind and endpoint travel because a
  -- reader holding one of these rows should not have to go and fetch what it is.
  (SELECT to_jsonb(s) FROM source s) AS source,

  -- The domain row, cut to the members the nodes below read. feature_version is the
  -- one that has to travel: a document written on this path is read against the same
  -- pin ar-ingest writes, and fetching one integer separately is the lookup node this
  -- shape exists to avoid. NULL rather than an empty object when nothing resolved,
  -- which is the same discriminator domain_id carries.
  (SELECT jsonb_build_object(
     'id', d.id,
     'slug', d.slug,
     'name', d.name,
     'settings', d.settings,
     'feature_version', d.feature_version,
     'embedding_model', d.embedding_model)
     FROM domains d
    WHERE d.id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)) AS domain,

  -- The personas. system_text is operator-owned prose and is the trusted half of what
  -- prompt-frame.ts composes around an untrusted chunk. No node on this canvas makes
  -- a model call, so nothing here reads them today; they are selected because the
  -- design fixes personas and taxonomy as what this node fetches, and because a
  -- capture that grows a judging step should not grow a second lookup with it.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', p.id,
       'role', p.role,
       'system_text', p.system_text)
       ORDER BY p.role, p.id)
       FROM personas p
      WHERE p.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS personas,

  -- The categories, which are the buckets the terms below are filed under. key rather
  -- than id is what a reader downstream matches on: features.ts builds a column name
  -- out of it and static-gate.ts groups hits by it, so the surrogate id travels for
  -- an operator's benefit and the key is what the libraries read.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', c.id,
       'key', c.key,
       'name', c.name,
       'parent_id', c.parent_id)
       ORDER BY c.key, c.id)
       FROM categories c
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS categories,

  -- The terms, joined to their category's key rather than carrying category_id. Four
  -- members and this exact spelling, because three libraries read this one list and
  -- each reads a different subset of it: static-gate.ts takes pattern, weight and
  -- polarity, features.ts takes pattern and category, and feature-version.ts takes
  -- all four. A term list selected without the join satisfies the first reader and
  -- starves the other two, with nothing failing.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'category', c.key,
       'pattern', t.pattern,
       'weight', t.weight,
       'polarity', t.polarity)
       ORDER BY c.key, t.pattern, t.id)
       FROM terms t
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = t.category_id
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS terms,

  -- The criteria, joined to their category the same way. Nothing on this canvas reads
  -- them: they are ar-score's subject, and the group that closes this pass hands that
  -- workflow the findings to score rather than this context, so it fetches its own.
  -- They are selected here because the taxonomy is these three tables, and a node
  -- group added below reads them without a second lookup.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', k.id,
       'category', c.key,
       'value', k.value,
       'kind', k.kind)
       ORDER BY c.key, k.kind, k.id)
       FROM criteria k
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = k.category_id
      WHERE k.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM source)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS criteria

WITH
-- The first thing this canvas does with the request, and it does it before anything
-- has judged the request. No member of the body has been read except the source id
-- the node above took out of it, and this statement writes the whole of it into
-- documents.raw with a parse_status of failed. Nothing below re-runs the write: the
-- group that reads the envelope, and the group that extracts under it, both act on
-- the row this statement left.

-- That ordering is the point rather than a convenience. A push source cannot be
-- re-read. A feed that answered something unusable is fetched again on the next pass,
-- so a refusal there costs one cycle; a capture refused before it was stored is gone,
-- and whoever posted it has already moved on. src/lib/capture-contract.ts states the
-- same rule from the other side, and every sentence it returns lands in
-- documents.parse_error on a row that already exists.

-- Three parameters, in declaration order: the domain the claimed source resolved to,
-- the source id the envelope claimed, and the request body as one jsonb. The body
-- binds as one value rather than as several because none of its members has been
-- judged, and a capture body is a bare string or a list as readily as an object.
-- JSON.stringify makes valid jsonb of all three, and the nullif is what puts a
-- request carrying no body back to SQL NULL rather than the JSON null literal.
posted AS (
  SELECT
    $1::bigint AS domain_id,
    $2::bigint AS source_id,
    nullif($3::jsonb, 'null'::jsonb) AS raw
),

-- The key this row stands on until the extraction below produces the real one.
-- documents.hash is NOT NULL and UNIQUE, and the digest that column eventually
-- carries is over a url and a body, neither of which has been read yet. So the row is
-- keyed provisionally, on the posted body as jsonb renders it, under a prefix no
-- content digest can hold: a content digest is 64 hexadecimal characters, and the
-- colon is the whole of the guarantee.

-- jsonb rather than the bytes as they arrived, deliberately. Two requests differing
-- only in the order of their keys or in their whitespace are one capture, and jsonb
-- renders both the same way, so the key collapses them into one row.

-- What that collapse covers is a second POST arriving before the first has been
-- promoted. It is not the repeat-capture guard, which is documents.hash own job and
-- happens one group below under the content digest: a promoted row carries that
-- digest by then, and a second POST of the same envelope conflicts with nothing here.
-- Both windows are covered and neither loses a payload. A row still carrying this
-- prefix is one nothing promoted, and its parse_error says which of the three that
-- was: a pass that stopped before the boundary, a source whose parser config could
-- not be read, or a reading of an item this corpus already holds. Only the first is a
-- row that re-POSTing finishes, the other two having run to the end and answered.

-- Two conditions are what confine this statement to captures there is somewhere to
-- put. documents.domain_id is NOT NULL, so an envelope naming a source this
-- deployment does not hold has no corpus to be written to, which is the reading Load
-- Domain Context answers and leaves to this group. A request carrying no body at all
-- has nothing to store, and a row recording it would say a document was captured when
-- what happened was that somebody reached the endpoint. Neither is dropped in
-- silence: the outer SELECT still answers its one item, with no document id and a
-- sentence saying which of the two it was.
candidate AS (
  SELECT
    p.domain_id,
    p.source_id,
    p.raw,
    'pending-capture:'
      || encode(sha256(convert_to(p.raw::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex') AS hash
  FROM posted p
  WHERE p.domain_id IS NOT NULL
    AND p.raw IS NOT NULL
),

-- The write. parse_status is written rather than left to its default, and what it is
-- written to is failed. The column defaults to ok and its own comment says what that
-- default cannot tell apart; here the honest answer is neither of those. Nothing has
-- read this payload, so ok would be a claim no writer on this path can make, and a
-- failure carrying its reason is the state the row is actually in until the boundary
-- below says otherwise.

-- parse_error is a constant sentence and carries nothing off the request. The no-echo
-- rule capture-contract.ts states is total on this path, and the reason is sharper
-- here than anywhere else on these canvases: this text is written from a body no
-- boundary has judged, so a template with a hole in it would put a stranger's value
-- into a column an operator reads. The whole body is in raw beside it, which is where
-- a value belongs.

-- url is NULL and body is the empty string, and both are placeholders the extraction
-- below writes over. documents.body is NOT NULL and may still be empty, which its own
-- comment argues at length: an empty body is a capture that yielded no text and was
-- kept anyway. Here it is a capture nothing has tried to read yet.

-- captured_at is left to its default, which is now. That column is when the pipeline
-- captured the document, and for a push that is the moment this row was written. The
-- client's own capturedAt is a claim inside an envelope nothing has judged, so it
-- stays in raw, and once the boundary has accepted it, it travels into the provenance
-- note src/sources/push-capture.ts records.

-- DO NOTHING is what makes the collapse above write no second row, and the conflict
-- target is the constraint by NAME rather than the column list, so renaming the
-- constraint breaks this statement instead of quietly arbitrating on something else.
written AS (
  INSERT INTO documents (
    domain_id, source_id, hash, url, body, raw, parse_status, parse_error)
  SELECT
    c.domain_id,
    c.source_id,
    c.hash,
    NULL::text,
    '',
    c.raw,
    'failed',
    'the capture was stored before validation and nothing has judged it since'
  FROM candidate c
  ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT documents_hash_unique DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id
)

SELECT
-- ONE ROW OUT, whatever happened. The insert sits in a CTE and this SELECT names no
-- FROM, so the node answers exactly one item for the one item it was handed. A
-- capture that was stored, a second POST that wrote nothing, and a request there was
-- no row to write each answer one item, and every group below reads a document id
-- rather than counting what reached it.

-- document_id is the row this capture is in, whether or not this pass is what put it
-- there. COALESCE reads it out of the insert when there was one and out of the corpus
-- when there was not, and only one of the two can ever answer: this query reads the
-- snapshot the statement began under, so it cannot see the row the CTE just wrote.
-- NULL means there is no row at all, which is one of the two refusals above.

-- document_stored is the other half of that pair and answers a different question. A
-- second POST of a capture already standing is a request that worked and wrote
-- nothing, so a reader counting new material reads this flag while a reader following
-- a document reads the id, and neither has to infer its answer from the other.

-- store_error says which refusal it was, and it is a constant either way. It is not
-- documents.parse_error and must not be read as one: that column is about a payload
-- that was stored and not read, where this is about a request there was nowhere to
-- store. The group below refuses the capture on it, and the group that closes the
-- pass records it.

-- The branches are read body first, and the order is the whole of what an operator is
-- told. Load Domain Context takes the source id out of the posted body, so a request
-- carrying no body always resolves no source as well: read the other way round, every
-- bodyless request would be reported as one naming a source this deployment does not
-- hold, which is a sentence about a claim nobody made. The narrower reason is the
-- true one, and it goes first.

-- The context is not echoed forward. This node's answer REPLACES Load Domain
-- Context's, and the source row, the domain row and the taxonomy are read back off
-- $('Load Domain Context').first().json by whichever node needs them. One request is
-- one item here, so a name is a safer handle than a copy able to disagree with the
-- row it was taken from.
  (SELECT domain_id FROM posted) AS domain_id,
  (SELECT source_id FROM posted) AS source_id,
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT w.id FROM written w),
    (SELECT d.id FROM documents d JOIN candidate c ON c.hash = d.hash))
    AS document_id,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM written) AS document_stored,
  CASE
    WHEN (SELECT raw FROM posted) IS NULL
    THEN 'the request carried no body to store'
    WHEN (SELECT domain_id FROM posted) IS NULL
    THEN 'the request named no source row this deployment holds'
  END AS store_error

WITH
-- Where the boundary's verdict becomes a row, and where an accepted envelope's
-- provenance is recorded. One statement writes both, because they are one fact about
-- one document: what this service decided about the capture, and the note the capture
-- carried about how it was taken.

-- ONE PARAMETER, the item itself, which is the shape every write on these canvases
-- uses. Fewer values for the comma splitter to get wrong than a member per column,
-- and the members are read out below where a comment can say what each one is instead
-- of inside an expression no gate reads. The note and the record are a JSONB object
-- in their own right, so binding the item whole is also the only spelling that keeps
-- them one.

-- ONE ROW OUT PER ITEM. The update sits in a CTE and the outer SELECT reads the row
-- the parameter made, so this node answers exactly one item for the one item it was
-- handed whether or not the update matched anything. An UPDATE ... RETURNING on its
-- own would emit nothing where it matched nothing, and the item would leave the
-- stream at exactly the point where the write not landing is the thing worth
-- reporting: a capture there was nowhere to store still has a verdict, and the group
-- that closes this pass is what records it.
item AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS payload
),

-- The members, cast once. The ids arrive as the node above carried them and are not
-- re-derived here, which is the rule every node on this canvas follows. Each of the
-- three may be NULL, and a JSON null reads through ->> as SQL NULL and casts to NULL
-- rather than raising, so a request there was nothing to store needs no guard of its
-- own.

-- capture_raw is the note and the record the node above built, taken only where it is
-- a JSON object. An absent member and a JSON null both answer something else to
-- jsonb_typeof, so both come through as SQL NULL rather than as a note of nothing: a
-- JavaScript null bound inside a JSONB value is the JSON null literal and not SQL
-- NULL, which is the trap this reading exists for. NULL here is a refused envelope,
-- and it is what leaves documents.raw as it was posted.

-- parse_error is what documents.parse_error should now say: the boundary's own
-- sentences joined, or the constant that says an accepted envelope is standing with
-- nothing extracted from it yet. Every spelling of it is a constant out of
-- src/lib/capture-contract.ts or out of the node above, and none of them carries a
-- value off the request. nullif over the empty string is the usual reading for a text
-- member: '' is a value, and a reader handed it sees a failure with no account of
-- itself.
verdict AS (
  SELECT
    (i.payload ->> 'domain_id')::bigint AS domain_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'source_id')::bigint AS source_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'document_id')::bigint AS document_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'document_stored')::boolean AS document_stored,
    i.payload ->> 'store_error' AS store_error,
    (i.payload ->> 'contract_version')::integer AS contract_version,
    (i.payload ->> 'contract_version_accepted')::boolean
      AS contract_version_accepted,
    (i.payload ->> 'envelope_accepted')::boolean AS envelope_accepted,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(i.payload -> 'capture_raw') = 'object'
         THEN i.payload -> 'capture_raw'
    END AS capture_raw,
    nullif(i.payload ->> 'parse_error', '') AS parse_error
  FROM item i
),

-- The write. Two columns move and no others: what this service now says about the
-- capture, and, for an accepted envelope, the note that says how the client took it.

-- COALESCE is the whole of the difference between the two verdicts. An accepted
-- envelope replaces documents.raw with the note and the record together, which is the
-- two member shape src/sources/push-capture.ts stores, and nothing is lost by the
-- move because the record IS the body that was posted. A refused one carries no note,
-- so raw stays exactly as it arrived: unexamined members rearranged under names
-- claiming they were read would be this statement asserting something no boundary
-- said.

-- documents.hash is not touched and does not need to be. Store Raw Capture keyed the
-- row provisionally over the body as posted, and that key is a column rather than a
-- derivation, so rewriting raw underneath it moves nothing. A second POST of the same
-- capture computes the same provisional key and lands on this same row.

-- parse_status is not touched either. The row is still failed, and it should be: an
-- accepted envelope is one nothing has extracted from yet, and the group below is
-- what promotes the status once it has. What changes here is only the account the row
-- gives of itself.

-- Two conditions confine the write. A NULL document_id is a capture there was no row
-- to write, which Store Raw Capture answered and this node acts on by matching
-- nothing: an item still comes out, saying so. And a NULL parse_error would blank the
-- column rather than fill it, so the row is left alone and the flag below reports
-- that the verdict did not land.
written AS (
  UPDATE documents d
     SET raw = COALESCE(v.capture_raw, d.raw),
         parse_error = v.parse_error
    FROM verdict v
   WHERE d.id = v.document_id
     AND v.parse_error IS NOT NULL
  RETURNING d.id
)

SELECT
-- The item this node answers, which is about the capture rather than about the write.
-- The ids and the store's own two members travel because the group that closes this
-- pass reads its counts off what came through here, and because a refusal higher up
-- is still a thing that happened to this request.

-- contract_version is what this service accepts, and contract_version_accepted is
-- whether the payload stated it. The pair is what tells a client author on the wrong
-- contract that the version is the thing to fix, and neither member repeats back what
-- was posted. envelope_accepted beside them is the whole verdict, and the group below
-- reads it to decide whether there is a body worth extracting from.

-- parse_error is what the column now says, echoed onto the item so a reader following
-- one execution does not have to go and fetch the row to find out. It is a constant
-- either way.

-- verdict_recorded and provenance_recorded answer two questions and neither is
-- inferred from the other. The first is whether the update matched a row at all,
-- which is false for a capture there was nowhere to store. The second is whether that
-- write was the one that put a note on the row, which is false again for every
-- refused envelope. A reader counting stored provenance reads the second, a reader
-- asking whether this pass reached the corpus at all reads the first.

-- The body is not echoed forward. The node below reads it off
-- $('Judge Capture Envelope').first().json.capture_raw, which is where the accepted
-- record and its note already sit together, so a capture's payload crosses this
-- connection once rather than on every item beneath it.
  v.domain_id,
  v.source_id,
  v.document_id,
  v.document_stored,
  v.store_error,
  v.contract_version,
  v.contract_version_accepted,
  v.envelope_accepted,
  v.parse_error,
  (SELECT w.id FROM written w) IS NOT NULL AS verdict_recorded,
  (SELECT w.id FROM written w) IS NOT NULL
    AND v.capture_raw IS NOT NULL AS provenance_recorded
FROM verdict v

WITH
-- Where a reading becomes the row it belongs to, and the promotion the store group
-- left for it. documents.parse_status moves off failed, and the hash, url and body
-- the extraction produced are written over the placeholders Store Raw Capture put
-- there. Nothing is inserted: that node wrote the row before any node had judged the
-- request, and this statement is the same row moved on rather than written again.

-- THREE OUTCOMES AND ONE ABSENCE, and the difference between them is what this
-- statement writes. A capture nothing could be read for leaves the row exactly as the
-- boundary group left it, carrying that group sentence and the posted body beside it.
-- A source whose parser config could not be read has its account updated and its
-- placeholders left alone, there being no reading to put in them. A reading gets the
-- key, the two columns and the status the extraction decided, ok when the source
-- contract was satisfied and failed with the divergences when it was not. And a
-- reading of something this corpus already holds keeps its provisional key and says
-- so.

-- THE KEY MOVES, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THAT LAST CASE NECESSARY. documents.hash is
-- UNIQUE and the digest written here is over the reading rather than over the posted
-- body, so a capture of an item already in the corpus would raise a unique violation
-- and take the pass down at exactly the point where a repeat capture is the ordinary
-- outcome. The key is therefore moved only where no other row carries it, and where
-- one does the row keeps the provisional key it was stored under and reports which
-- document it repeats.

-- The edge of that rule is worth naming rather than meeting. A reading that produced
-- neither a url nor a body hashes the same as any other reading that produced
-- neither, so the second of those is reported as a repeat of the first. That is the
-- dedupe rule documents.hash states, read at its edge rather than a defect of this
-- statement, and the row still stands with the whole capture in raw beside it.

-- ONE ROW OUT, whatever happened. The update sits in a CTE and the outer SELECT reads
-- the row the parameter made, so this node answers exactly one item for the one item
-- it was handed whether or not it wrote anything. An UPDATE ... RETURNING on its own
-- emits nothing where it matched nothing, and the item would leave the stream at
-- exactly the point where the write not landing is the thing worth reporting.

-- ONE PARAMETER, the item itself, which is the shape every write on these canvases
-- uses. Fewer values for the comma splitter to get wrong than a member per column,
-- and the members are read out below where a comment can say what each one is instead
-- of inside an expression no gate reads.
item AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS payload
),

-- The whitespace run the hash basis collapses, spelled out rather than left to the
-- shorthand class. Postgres reads that shorthand as ASCII whitespace and JavaScript
-- reads it, under the u flag, as the Unicode set, so the two disagree about a
-- non-breaking space and about a byte order mark sitting inside a body.
-- src/sources/push-capture.ts computes the same digest Node side and ar-ingest
-- computes it in SQL, and all three writers share one unique key: a class differing
-- by a single code point is two rows for one item on every document reached more than
-- one way.
whitespace AS (
  SELECT '[\u0009\u000a\u000b\u000c\u000d\u0020\u00a0\u1680'
      || '\u2000\u2001\u2002\u2003\u2004\u2005\u2006\u2007'
      || '\u2008\u2009\u200a\u2028\u2029\u202f\u205f\u3000'
      || '\ufeff]+' AS run
),

-- The members, cast once. The ids arrive as the nodes above carried them and are not
-- re-derived here, which is the rule every node on this canvas follows. Each may be
-- NULL, and a JSON null reads through the text operator as SQL NULL and casts to NULL
-- rather than raising, so a request there was nothing to store needs no guard of its
-- own.

-- record is the reading, taken only where it is a JSON object. An absent member and a
-- JSON null both answer something else to jsonb_typeof, so both come through as SQL
-- NULL rather than as a reading of nothing: a JavaScript null bound inside a JSONB
-- value is the JSON null literal and not SQL NULL, which is the trap this reading
-- exists for. NULL here is a capture nothing was extracted from, and it is what
-- leaves the placeholders alone.

-- parse_status and parse_error are what the extraction decided, and this statement
-- does not revisit either. The contract was read up there, beside the config that
-- directed the reading, and a second judgment down here would be a copy with nothing
-- comparing it against the first. A NULL status is the one case where nothing is
-- written at all.

-- finding_fields passes straight through to the node below. It is not read here and
-- not written here: findings is that node table, and carrying the payload on the item
-- is what keeps this canvas one main chain with one item on it.
verdict AS (
  SELECT
    (i.payload ->> 'domain_id')::bigint AS domain_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'source_id')::bigint AS source_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'document_id')::bigint AS document_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'document_stored')::boolean AS document_stored,
    i.payload ->> 'store_error' AS store_error,
    (i.payload ->> 'contract_version')::integer AS contract_version,
    (i.payload ->> 'contract_version_accepted')::boolean
      AS contract_version_accepted,
    (i.payload ->> 'envelope_accepted')::boolean AS envelope_accepted,
    i.payload ->> 'parse_status' AS parse_status,
    nullif(i.payload ->> 'parse_error', '') AS parse_error,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(i.payload -> 'record') = 'object'
         THEN i.payload -> 'record'
    END AS record,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(i.payload -> 'finding_fields') = 'object'
         THEN i.payload -> 'finding_fields'
    END AS finding_fields,
    nullif(i.payload ->> 'finding_refusal', '') AS finding_refusal
  FROM item i
),

-- The two columns a documents row takes from the reading, read off the field map by
-- name, and the digest that keys the row. url and body are the field names both
-- adapters under src/sources/ write, and that convention is the whole of the mapping:
-- naming a field map members after the columns costs an operator one sentence of
-- documentation, where a second mapping from field names to column names would be
-- another config to get wrong.

-- A member that is not a string is not text whatever it coerced to, so a numeric url
-- reads as no url rather than as a link to a number. The empty string is an absence
-- for url, which is NULL where there is no such place and never the empty string, and
-- a value for body, which is NOT NULL and may still be empty: a capture that yielded
-- no text was kept anyway.

-- The basis is the url and the body, each with its whitespace runs collapsed and its
-- ends trimmed, JSON encoded into a two member array so that the halves cannot bleed
-- into each other: without the encoding a url ending in the first words of a body
-- would collide with a shorter url and a longer one. What is left OUT of it is the
-- half that does the work. The source is not in the basis, deliberately, because
-- documents.hash exists so that capturing the same item a second way lands on the row
-- already there rather than beside it. Neither is the capture stamp, nor the
-- provenance, nor the domain.

-- The digest is computed only where there is a reading. Over no reading at all it
-- would be the digest of two empty strings, which is a key rather than an absence,
-- and every capture whose config could not be read would collide on it.
reading AS (
  SELECT
    v.document_id,
    member.url,
    member.body,
    CASE WHEN v.record IS NOT NULL
         THEN encode(sha256(convert_to(
           '[' || to_json(collapsed.url)::text
               || ',' || to_json(collapsed.body)::text || ']',
           'UTF8')), 'hex')
    END AS hash
  FROM verdict v
  CROSS JOIN whitespace ws
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT
      nullif(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(v.record -> 'url') = 'string'
                  THEN v.record ->> 'url'
             END, '') AS url,
      COALESCE(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(v.record -> 'body') = 'string'
                    THEN v.record ->> 'body'
               END, '') AS body) AS member
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT
      btrim(regexp_replace(
        COALESCE(member.url, ''), ws.run, ' ', 'g'), ' ') AS url,
      btrim(regexp_replace(
        member.body, ws.run, ' ', 'g'), ' ') AS body) AS collapsed
),

-- Whether another row already carries this digest. documents.hash is UNIQUE, so the
-- subquery answers at most one row by construction and needs no bound of its own. The
-- row this capture is standing in is excluded, which is what keeps a promotion from
-- reporting itself: it still carries its provisional key at this point, so the
-- exclusion only matters once, on a re-run over a row this pass already promoted.
standing AS (
  SELECT
    r.document_id,
    r.url,
    r.body,
    r.hash,
    (SELECT o.id
       FROM documents o
      WHERE o.hash = r.hash
        AND o.id IS DISTINCT FROM r.document_id) AS duplicate_of
  FROM reading r
),

-- What the three columns should be. hash is NULL for a duplicate and for a capture
-- with no reading, and that one member is the whole discriminator the update below
-- reads: where it is NULL the key, the url and the body are all left where they are.

-- The status and the sentence a duplicate gets are this statement own, and they are
-- constants. The row is a capture that arrived, was stored, was accepted by the
-- boundary and turned out to be an item the corpus already holds, which is a readable
-- state rather than an error: what is in it is the whole posted body, and the
-- document it repeats is named on the item this node answers.
promotion AS (
  SELECT
    s.document_id,
    s.url,
    s.body,
    s.duplicate_of,
    CASE WHEN s.duplicate_of IS NULL THEN s.hash END AS hash,
    CASE WHEN s.duplicate_of IS NOT NULL
         THEN 'failed'
         ELSE v.parse_status
    END AS parse_status,
    CASE WHEN s.duplicate_of IS NOT NULL
         THEN 'the reading duplicates a document this corpus already holds'
         ELSE v.parse_error
    END AS parse_error
  FROM standing s
  CROSS JOIN verdict v
),

-- The write. Five columns and no others, and two conditions confine it.

-- A NULL parse_status is a capture nothing was extracted from, which is an envelope
-- the boundary refused or a request there was no row to write. Both were recorded by
-- the group above on the row itself, so this statement matches nothing and says so;
-- overwriting parse_error with a NULL would blank an account that is already correct.

-- A NULL hash is a reading there is none of, or one this corpus already holds, and
-- the CASE arms are what leave the placeholders alone in both cases. The row still
-- gets its account of itself updated, which is the difference between the two
-- conditions: one says nothing happened, the other says something did and it was not
-- a promotion.

-- documents.raw is not touched. The boundary group replaced it with the note and the
-- record together for an accepted envelope, and that is the capture as it arrived;
-- this statement writes what was READ out of it and has nothing to add to the
-- evidence.
written AS (
  UPDATE documents d
     SET hash = COALESCE(p.hash, d.hash),
         url = CASE WHEN p.hash IS NULL THEN d.url ELSE p.url END,
         body = CASE WHEN p.hash IS NULL THEN d.body ELSE p.body END,
         parse_status = p.parse_status,
         parse_error = p.parse_error
    FROM promotion p
   WHERE d.id = p.document_id
     AND p.parse_status IS NOT NULL
  RETURNING d.id
)

SELECT
-- The item this node answers, which is about the capture rather than about the write.
-- The boundary members come through unchanged because a refusal higher up is still a
-- thing that happened to this request, and the group that closes this pass reads its
-- counts off them.

-- parse_status and parse_error are what the column now says, echoed onto the item so
-- a reader following one execution does not have to go and fetch the row. Every
-- spelling of the sentence is a constant or a list of them, and none carries a value
-- off the capture.

-- verdict_recorded and document_promoted answer two questions and neither is inferred
-- from the other. The first is whether the update matched a row at all, which is
-- false for a capture there was nowhere to store. The second is whether that write
-- moved the key, which is false again for a config that could not be read and for a
-- reading this corpus already holds. duplicate_of beside them names the document a
-- repeat capture landed on, and it is null for every other outcome.

-- finding_fields and finding_refusal travel one node further because the node below
-- is what writes them, and because a refusal reaches no column at all: findings has
-- nowhere to put a finding that was not made, so the group that closes this pass is
-- what records that there was one.
  v.domain_id,
  v.source_id,
  v.document_id,
  v.document_stored,
  v.store_error,
  v.contract_version,
  v.contract_version_accepted,
  v.envelope_accepted,
  p.parse_status,
  p.parse_error,
  p.duplicate_of,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM written) AS verdict_recorded,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM written) AND p.hash IS NOT NULL
    AS document_promoted,
  v.finding_fields,
  v.finding_refusal
FROM verdict v
CROSS JOIN promotion p

WITH
-- Where a validated reading becomes a row, and the last write this pass makes about
-- the document. The core columns are neutral and mean the same thing in every domain,
-- and everything this one needed beyond them is the fields payload the extraction
-- node checked against its contract. findings in src/db/schema/findings.ts argues
-- that split at length: it is what lets one table serve every domain, and neither
-- half works alone.

-- A REWRITE AND NOT A RENAME. The design this port draws from wrote its results into
-- a table whose columns were its subject matter, one column per thing that subject
-- happened to have, so a second subject was a migration and a query per subject.
-- Nothing of that shape survives here. What a domain needs beyond the neutral columns
-- is a key in the JSONB payload the domain itself declares, which is why this
-- statement names a domain, a document and a payload and names nothing that could
-- belong to one subject alone.

-- NO MODEL WROTE THIS PAYLOAD, which is the whole of what separates this node from
-- the one ar-ingest writes findings with. There the fields are a model answer, parsed
-- out of text and validated before anything stores it. Here they are the reading a
-- parser_config directed, validated against the same domain contract by the same
-- rules. The column cannot tell the two apart and does not need to: what
-- findings.fields promises is that the payload fits the domain declaration, and both
-- paths check it before writing.

-- TWO CONDITIONS, AND NEITHER IS THE OTHER. A finding is written where the domain
-- contract accepted the reading AND where the document this pass captured was
-- promoted to its own key. The first is about the payload. The second is about the
-- row: a capture of an item this corpus already holds kept a provisional key and
-- stands as a record of the request rather than as the document, so hanging a finding
-- off it would file this domain material under a row nothing else reads. What that
-- costs is a finding for a repeat capture, which the document it repeats already has
-- or already went without.

-- A REFUSED READING WRITES NOTHING AND RAISES NOTHING. The WHERE clause is the whole
-- of it: the document goes on standing exactly as it did, with its raw, its verdict
-- and its account of itself, and no finding hung off it. The sentence saying why sits
-- on the item and reaches no column, findings having nowhere to put a finding that
-- was not made.

-- ONE ROW OUT PER ITEM. The insert sits in a CTE and the outer SELECT reads the one
-- row the parameter made, so this node answers exactly one item whether or not it
-- wrote anything. An INSERT ... RETURNING on its own would emit nothing for a refused
-- reading, and the item would vanish from the stream at exactly the point where a
-- refusal is an ordinary outcome.

-- ONE PARAMETER, the item itself. Fewer values for the comma splitter to get wrong
-- than a member per column, and the members are read out below where a comment can
-- say what each one is instead of inside an expression no gate reads.
item AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS payload
),

-- The members, cast once. The ids arrive as the nodes above carried them and are not
-- re-derived here, which is the rule every node on this canvas follows: a value
-- copied forward can be wrong, and a value computed twice can disagree with itself.

-- fields is the payload the extraction node validated, or SQL NULL where it refused.
-- jsonb_typeof is what parts the two: an absent member and a JSON null both answer
-- something other than object, so both come through as NULL and neither reaches the
-- insert.

-- document_promoted is false for a capture there was nowhere to store as well as for
-- one this corpus already holds, so the second condition covers the first and
-- document_id needs no test of its own. It is NOT NULL on the table either way, which
-- reports a canvas contradicting itself loudly rather than quietly.
finding AS (
  SELECT
    (i.payload ->> 'domain_id')::bigint AS domain_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'source_id')::bigint AS source_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'document_id')::bigint AS document_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'document_promoted')::boolean AS document_promoted,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(i.payload -> 'finding_fields') = 'object'
         THEN i.payload -> 'finding_fields'
    END AS fields
  FROM item i
),

-- The write, and the columns it names are the whole of what this pass knows. Every
-- other one is left to the table, each for its own reason.

-- entity_id stays null, and null there is an ordinary state rather than a gap:
-- findings.entity_id says a finding is attributed when the pipeline can name the
-- subject behind it, and plenty are worth keeping without one. Nothing on this canvas
-- resolves an entity, and a placeholder subject to hang the unattributed ones off is
-- the exact shape that column refuses.

-- score and score_version stay null together, which findings.score_version asks for
-- in as many words: the two are written by one statement or by neither, and a score
-- stored with no version survives every re-score the pin exists to trigger. ar-score
-- is the statement that writes them, invoked by the group that closes this pass.

-- created_at takes its default, the insert being when the finding was made.

-- No ON CONFLICT clause, because there is no key to collide on. A document reaches
-- this node once per capture that promoted it, and a capture that promoted nothing
-- does not reach it at all.
written AS (
  INSERT INTO findings (domain_id, document_id, fields)
  SELECT f.domain_id, f.document_id, f.fields
  FROM finding f
  WHERE f.fields IS NOT NULL
    AND f.document_promoted
  RETURNING id
)

SELECT
-- The item this node answers, which is about the document rather than about the
-- write. The ids it arrived with travel on because the group that closes this pass is
-- charged to the capture and reads its counts off what came through here, and the
-- members that describe the capture itself are read back off the nodes above by name
-- rather than restated: a second copy of one of them could disagree with the first.

-- finding_id is the row this reading left behind, or null where there is none. That
-- null is the only reading of a refusal any node below has, and it does not say which
-- of the two refusals it was: a payload the domain contract turned away and a
-- document that was never promoted both answer it, and the two members that tell them
-- apart are on the nodes above.
  f.domain_id,
  f.source_id,
  f.document_id,
  (SELECT w.id FROM written w) AS finding_id
FROM finding f

WITH
-- Where four values become four columns, and the fail and flag halves of
-- fail-flag-keep written as one statement. Judge Capture Health decided them and
-- nothing here revisits the decision: the counter, the two stamps and the flag arrive
-- on the item and are written as they came. src/lib/source-health.ts holds the
-- arithmetic, the node above is where the outcome was read off this pass's single
-- reading, and a rule restated down here would be a copy with nothing comparing it
-- against the first.

-- BOTH STAMPS EVERY PASS, including the one that did not move. The answer above holds
-- four values and this statement is built from exactly those, so the stamp being
-- carried through is written back as it came. Writing only the one that moved would
-- mean working out down here which of them did, which is the decision taken a second
-- time in a second language. What the round trip costs is precision and nothing else:
-- the column holds microseconds and the item carried the value as JSON, so a
-- carried-through stamp is rewritten at the millisecond it survived as. Whether a
-- source is broken right now is read off which of the two stamps is the more recent,
-- and a millisecond parts no two passes.

-- ONE PARAMETER, the item itself, which is the shape every write on this canvas uses
-- and is where it parts from ar-ingest's twin of this node. There the six values bind
-- separately because the health group is one item per source; here a capture is one
-- request, so the item binds whole and the members are read out below where a comment
-- can say what each one is instead of inside an expression no gate reads.

-- A stamp the node above could not read as one arrives here as it came and the cast
-- refuses it, loudly, which is the right volume: a NULL written in its place would
-- claim the source has never once succeeded.

-- The write is blind and keyed on the id. The values it applies were worked out from
-- a row read at the top of this pass, and nothing here locks it, so two captures
-- posted against one source at the same moment would have the later write win and
-- lose the earlier bump. There is no claim upstream to lean on the way ar-ingest
-- leans on the dispatcher's SKIP LOCKED select: this workflow is started by whoever
-- posts to it, as often as they post. The cost is a counter short rather than a wrong
-- flag, both passes having read the same source row and judged their own capture, and
-- the flag survives every later pass once it is up.
item AS (
  SELECT $1::jsonb AS payload
),

-- The members, cast once. The ids arrive as the nodes above carried them and are not
-- re-derived here, which is the rule every node on this canvas follows. Each may be
-- NULL, and a JSON null reads through the text operator as SQL NULL and casts to NULL
-- rather than raising, so a capture with no source needs no guard of its own.

-- source_judged is what parts a source this pass decided nothing about from one it
-- decided a success about. Both leave the four members below unread by the update,
-- the first because they are null and the second because they are not, and only this
-- member says which.
verdict AS (
  SELECT
    (i.payload ->> 'domain_id')::bigint AS domain_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'source_id')::bigint AS source_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'document_id')::bigint AS document_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'finding_id')::bigint AS finding_id,
    (i.payload ->> 'source_judged')::boolean AS source_judged,
    (i.payload ->> 'consecutive_failures')::integer AS consecutive_failures,
    (i.payload ->> 'last_success_at')::timestamptz AS last_success_at,
    (i.payload ->> 'last_failure_at')::timestamptz AS last_failure_at,
    (i.payload ->> 'flagged')::boolean AS flagged
  FROM item i
),

-- The write. Two conditions confine it, and they are not one condition twice. The id
-- has to match a row, which is what a capture naming a source this deployment does
-- not hold fails; and the node above has to have judged something, which is what
-- keeps four nulls from being written over a real row on a pass that decided nothing.
-- Either alone admits the other case.
applied AS (
  UPDATE sources s
  -- FOUR COLUMNS AND NO FIFTH. enabled is not in this list and may not be. It is the
  -- operator's column outright, where flagged is the pipeline's own reading, and
  -- src/db/schema/sources.ts keeps the two apart so the rot detector cannot switch
  -- off a feed somebody deliberately turned on. The library answers exactly the four
  -- written here and carries no enabled member for the same reason: a column named in
  -- an answer is a column somebody eventually writes.

  -- flagged is set here and never cleared here, which is a property of the value
  -- rather than of this clause. The library sets it once the counter reaches the
  -- threshold and has no member that unsets it, so this statement can write false
  -- only for a source that was already false. Clearing a flag is an operator's act,
  -- taken once whatever broke has been fixed.
     SET consecutive_failures = v.consecutive_failures,
         last_success_at = v.last_success_at,
         last_failure_at = v.last_failure_at,
         flagged = v.flagged
    FROM verdict v
   WHERE s.id = v.source_id
     AND v.source_judged
  RETURNING s.consecutive_failures, s.flagged
)

SELECT
-- ONE ROW OUT, whatever happened. The update sits in a CTE and the outer SELECT reads
-- the row the parameter made, so this node answers exactly one item for the one item
-- it was handed. An UPDATE ... RETURNING on its own emits nothing when its WHERE
-- matches nothing, and the capture would leave the stream at the one point where the
-- write not landing is worth reporting.

-- health_applied is that case named, and source_judged beside it is what makes it
-- readable. False with source_judged false is a capture there was no source to judge.
-- False with source_judged true is a source row that is no longer there, which is a
-- source deleted mid pass rather than one that failed, and counting the two as one
-- thing is how a deletion turns into a flag nobody can explain.

-- The counter and the flag are read back out of the update rather than echoed from
-- the item, so what this node answers is what the row now holds. Nothing else about
-- the capture is restated: the boundary verdict, the reading, the promotion and the
-- finding stay on the nodes that decided them, where the statement that closes this
-- pass reaches them by name.

-- AND THE HAND-OVER, which this node carries because it is the last node before the
-- invocation and because a node whose only job was projection would be a fifth node
-- on a canvas that has nothing else to do. ar-ingest builds the same hand-over in the
-- node that raises its research intentions, for the same reason.

-- domain_id is what ar-score fetches its own criteria, terms and personas against. It
-- is the domain the claimed source resolved to, and it is NULL for a capture that
-- resolved none, which is the discriminator Load Domain Context puts on every item
-- here.

-- finding_ids is every finding this capture wrote, which is one or none. A list
-- rather than an id, because what ar-score is written to take is a list: a capture
-- and an ingest pass hand it the same shape, so that workflow has one first node
-- rather than one per caller.

-- capture_document_id is provenance, and the name is doing the same work
-- ingest_run_id does on ar-ingest's hand-over. This canvas opens no run row until the
-- node below it, so there is no run id to hand over at all, and what identifies a
-- capture is the document it was stored as. A member spelled run_id would be read by
-- the first node of a workflow written to resolve a domain out of exactly that
-- member, which is the mistake the name exists to prevent.
  v.domain_id,
  v.source_id,
  v.source_judged,
  (SELECT a.consecutive_failures FROM applied a) AS consecutive_failures,
  (SELECT a.flagged FROM applied a) AS flagged,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM applied) AS health_applied,
  v.document_id AS capture_document_id,
  CASE WHEN v.finding_id IS NULL
       THEN '[]'::jsonb
       ELSE jsonb_build_array(v.finding_id)
  END AS finding_ids
FROM verdict v

nodes.name: Score Capture Findings
nodes.notes: Hands ar-score the findings this capture produced and waits for it. Run once with all items rather than once for each, which on this canvas is a claim about the shape rather than a saving: every node here answers exactly one item for the one request, so the two modes would open the same single sub-execution and the once mode is what says the item IS the hand-over rather than one of a batch. Waiting is what lets Close Capture Run below write the pass account after the scoring is done rather than while it runs, the same reason ar-ingest's Score Findings waits. The item is the hand-over: domain_id says which domain's criteria to score against, finding_ids says exactly which rows and is empty for every capture that wrote none, and capture_document_id is provenance under a name that cannot be mistaken for a run this workflow opened, since this canvas opens none until the node below and ar-score closes a runs row of its own. An empty finding_ids is not a reason to skip the call: what a scoring pass does with nothing to score is that workflow's answer, and a branch here would be this canvas deciding it. onError continues on the REGULAR output instead of raising, because a scoring pass that could not start must not cost this capture its own account of itself: the failure stays on the item and Close Capture Run reads it, writes the run partial and records an entry naming this node. alwaysOutputData is the other half of that, for the case that is not an error at all: a sub-workflow returning no items would otherwise leave this node with nothing on its output, and the pass would end at the node built to account for it. The id resolves through AR_SCORE_WORKFLOW_ID in scripts/workflow-markers.ts, so a setting nothing answers for fails the build rather than an execution.

parameters.query:
WITH
-- Where the pass says what it did, and the one node on this canvas that writes a runs
-- row at all. runs in src/db/schema/runs.ts keeps that account in three columns
-- because a reader wanting any one of them should not have to parse the other two:
-- status is what the pass came to, counts is what it did, and errors is what it could
-- not do. This statement writes all three and the finish beside them.

-- IT INSERTS WHERE ar-ingest UPDATES, and that is the whole of how this node differs
-- from its twin. A dispatched pass arrives with a run id: ar-dispatch opened the row
-- before it invoked anything, and ar-ingest closes the row it was handed. A capture
-- arrives as a POST from a stranger and nothing has opened anything, so the row is
-- written once, here, already closed. runs.started_at names exactly this convention
-- as the one the design this port draws from uses, and says in as many words that
-- nothing stored tells the two apart. What it costs is the duration: started_at
-- defaults to now() in the same transaction that sets finished_at, so a capture run
-- reads as instantaneous. What it keeps is the ordering and the account, which is
-- what this table is read for. The obvious repair, dating the start from
-- documents.captured_at, is wrong rather than merely more work: a second POST of a
-- standing capture would date this run from the first one, days earlier.

-- SCHEDULED_BY IS operator, AND IT IS A CONVENTION RATHER THAN A READING.
-- RUN_SCHEDULERS in src/db/schema/values.ts answers who set the next_run_at a run
-- fired against, and a capture fired against none: all three members are wrong of it,
-- and operator is the least wrong, this pass having happened because something
-- outside this system acted rather than because a clock came due. ar-dispatch's Open
-- Run left this phase a choice between a column naming the workflow that opened a row
-- and a second convention, and this is the second convention: that statement writes
-- the literal interval for every row it opens and this one writes operator, so a row
-- saying interval is a dispatched pass and a row saying operator is one nothing
-- scheduled. Its limits are exactly the limits of a convention, and it has already
-- stopped telling one workflow from another. ar-score reached the same question at
-- its own closing node and answered it the same way for the same reason, so a row
-- saying operator is a capture or a scoring pass rather than a capture. What still
-- tells those two apart is counts, whose keys are the writer's: a capture row carries
-- captures_received and a scoring row carries findings_handed. The column that would
-- answer it properly is a migration this phase does not carry.

-- ONE ROW PER REQUEST, which is a real cost and is worth naming rather than meeting.
-- A capture client posting a hundred pages a day writes a hundred runs rows, where a
-- pull domain writes one a tick. Nothing here batches them, because nothing here can:
-- the pass IS the request, and a row covering several would have to be opened by
-- something that knew they were coming. What it buys is the thing runs exists for,
-- that a source which quietly stopped working arrives on the next digest as a banner
-- rather than as a silence nobody thinks to investigate.

-- THE TALLIES ARE COUNTED HERE AND GATHERED THERE. The parameter below carries one
-- object per node, each cut to the members a tally reads, and every rule about what
-- those members MEAN is in this statement. An expression can import nothing and is
-- read by no gate in this repository, so a rule written there would be a second copy
-- of something with nowhere to be compared. Naming and projection are what the
-- expression does.

-- IT READS MEMBERS WHERE ar-ingest's Close Run NORMALISES LISTS, and the difference
-- is the canvas rather than a preference. There every node answers one item per
-- source or per document, so the gathered pass is a set of arrays and a tally is a
-- count with a predicate. Here every node answers exactly one item for the one
-- request, so each tally is one condition and the arrays would be one element long:
-- jsonb_each over them would be machinery answering a question that has one answer.

-- AN ID IS TESTED AS TEXT AND NEVER BY TYPE. A bigint read as a top-level column
-- comes back off the driver as a STRING, so document_id, duplicate_of and finding_id
-- all arrive spelled "41" while an integer column arrives as the number 41. A test
-- written on jsonb_typeof would answer for one spelling and miss the other, which is
-- a count wrong by a plausible amount rather than one that fails. Every id predicate
-- below reads the member's TEXT, which is the same either way and is NULL for an
-- absent member and for a JSON null. A boolean is compared as jsonb, which needs no
-- cast at all, and every one of those comparisons is wrapped in a COALESCE: a member
-- that never arrived compares to UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN in the status CASE below would
-- fall through to a branch nobody chose.

-- NOTHING HERE CAN RAISE, which matters more at this node than anywhere else on the
-- canvas: this is where the pass records itself, and a statement that threw would
-- leave a capture with no account at all. So the gathered object is guarded before it
-- is read, every member is read with an operator that answers NULL rather than
-- raising on a shape it did not expect, and no list is expanded in a FROM clause.

-- WHAT MAKES A PASS partial, failed OR ok. RUN_STATUSES in src/db/schema/values.ts
-- argues partial as the member fail-flag-keep needs: a pass that produced real work
-- and a real failure at once, where either neighbour loses half of it. Read onto one
-- capture, it is a document that was promoted under a source that failed, which is a
-- reading the source contract turned away and the corpus kept anyway. failed is the
-- narrower case where there is no half to keep: a request there was nowhere to store,
-- and a source failure that promoted nothing, which is every refused envelope and
-- every unreadable parser_config. A repeat capture is ok rather than either: the
-- source answered in the shape it promised and the corpus already holds the item,
-- which is a client working.

-- WHAT DOES NOT MAKE IT PARTIAL is a reading the domain field contract turned away.
-- The capture was posted, stored, judged, promoted and keyed before that check ran,
-- each of those left a row, and a payload that does not fit what this domain declares
-- its findings hold says nothing about the source that sent it. It is counted, under
-- answers_refused, and counting it is what a tally is for.

-- THE ERRORS ENTRIES ARE ONE PER FAILURE and are ASSIGNED rather than appended.
-- runs.errors defaults to an empty list and this row is new, so there is nobody
-- else's account of the same run to drop: ar-ingest appends because ar-dispatch
-- opened its row and may write to it. Every sentence that reaches this column is a
-- constant out of src/lib/capture-contract.ts, out of src/lib/parser-config.ts, or
-- out of a node above, and none of them carries a value off the request. The field
-- names a config fault reports are the operator's own, written in a sources row
-- rather than posted by a stranger.

-- RUNS ONCE FOR THE PASS. executeOnce is set on this node, so it writes one row
-- however many items Score Capture Findings above answered with, that count being
-- whatever ar-score returned rather than anything this canvas fixes.

-- EVERY REQUEST REACHES THIS NODE, which is a property this canvas has and ar-ingest
-- does not. Every node between the trigger and here answers exactly one item whatever
-- it decided, the writes sitting in CTEs under outer SELECTs that name no FROM, so
-- there is no branch on which a capture stops early and leaves no account of itself.
-- The one way a pass ends without a row is a node raising, which is what the guards
-- above are about.

-- TWO PARAMETERS, in declaration order: the gathered pass, and the error Score
-- Capture Findings kept in the stream if its invocation did not complete. The error
-- is stringified on the way in for the reason ar-dispatch's Close Run Failed
-- stringifies its own: a parameter is split on commas unless it parses as JSON on its
-- own, and an executor's message routinely carries one.
pass AS (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof($1::jsonb) = 'object'
         THEN $1::jsonb
         ELSE '{}'::jsonb
    END AS nodes,
    nullif($2::jsonb, 'null'::jsonb) AS score_error
),

-- The pass read out one member at a time, and this is where every shape this
-- statement is not going to trust is turned into one it can. A member the expression
-- never set reads as NULL through the object operator, so an absent node is an absent
-- reading rather than a raise, and each of the booleans below is a COALESCE so that
-- an absent reading is a false rather than an UNKNOWN travelling into the CASE that
-- decides the status.

-- document_exists is the discriminator the status leans on hardest. It is true for a
-- capture this pass stored and for a second POST that landed on one already standing,
-- and false only where there was nowhere to put the request at all: no body, or a
-- source id this deployment does not hold.

-- record_status is the extraction's verdict rather than the promotion's, the same
-- member Judge Capture Health read its own outcome off, so a reading this corpus
-- already holds is not counted as a refused one.
capture AS (
  SELECT
    p.score_error,
    CASE WHEN (p.nodes #>> '{context,domain_id}') ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
         THEN (p.nodes #>> '{context,domain_id}')::bigint
    END AS domain_id,
    COALESCE((p.nodes #>> '{store,document_id}') ~ '^[0-9]+$', false)
      AS document_exists,
    COALESCE(p.nodes #> '{store,document_stored}' = 'true'::jsonb, false)
      AS document_written,
    nullif(p.nodes #>> '{store,store_error}', '') AS store_error,
    COALESCE(p.nodes #> '{envelope,envelope_accepted}' = 'true'::jsonb, false)
      AS envelope_accepted,
    p.nodes #> '{envelope,contract_version}' AS contract_version,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(p.nodes #> '{envelope,capture_faults}') = 'array'
         THEN p.nodes #> '{envelope,capture_faults}'
         ELSE '[]'::jsonb
    END AS capture_faults,
    p.nodes #>> '{records,parse_status}' AS record_status,
    CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(p.nodes #> '{records,config_errors}') = 'array'
         THEN p.nodes #> '{records,config_errors}'
         ELSE '[]'::jsonb
    END AS config_errors,
    COALESCE(p.nodes #> '{promote,document_promoted}' = 'true'::jsonb, false)
      AS document_promoted,
    COALESCE((p.nodes #>> '{promote,duplicate_of}') ~ '^[0-9]+$', false)
      AS document_repeated,
    nullif(p.nodes #>> '{promote,finding_refusal}', '') AS finding_refusal,
    COALESCE((p.nodes #>> '{finding,finding_id}') ~ '^[0-9]+$', false)
      AS finding_written,
    COALESCE(p.nodes #> '{health,source_judged}' = 'true'::jsonb, false)
      AS source_judged,
    COALESCE(p.nodes #> '{health,flagged}' = 'true'::jsonb, false)
      AS source_flagged,
    COALESCE((p.nodes #>> '{health,consecutive_failures}') ~ '^[0-9]+$'
      AND (p.nodes #>> '{health,consecutive_failures}')::integer > 0, false)
      AS source_failed,
    p.nodes #> '{health,source_id}' AS source_id,
    p.nodes #> '{health,consecutive_failures}' AS consecutive_failures
  FROM pass p
),

-- What the pass did, one count per question a reader of a digest asks. Every one of
-- them is nought or one here, a capture being one request, and the names are
-- ar-ingest's own wherever the question is the same: a digest reading counts should
-- not have to know which workflow wrote the row it is reading.

-- captures_received is the one that is always one, and it is what the others are read
-- against. Without it a row of zeros is indistinguishable from a row nobody filled
-- in.

-- documents_written is this pass having stored a row, where documents_repeated is the
-- reading having landed on an item the corpus already holds. They are not opposites
-- and a capture can be neither: a second POST arriving before the first was promoted
-- writes nothing and repeats nothing, having collapsed onto the provisional key
-- instead.
tally AS (
  SELECT
    1 AS captures_received,
    CASE WHEN c.source_judged THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS sources_read,
    CASE WHEN c.source_failed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS sources_failed,
    CASE WHEN c.source_flagged THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS sources_flagged,
    CASE WHEN c.envelope_accepted THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS envelopes_refused,
    CASE WHEN c.record_status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS records_refused,
    CASE WHEN c.document_written THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS documents_written,
    CASE WHEN c.document_promoted THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS documents_promoted,
    CASE WHEN c.document_repeated THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS documents_repeated,
    CASE WHEN c.finding_refusal IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS answers_refused,
    CASE WHEN c.finding_written THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS findings_written
  FROM capture c
),

-- What the pass could not do, one entry per failure, in the shape ar-dispatch's Close
-- Run Failed already writes: the node that met it and the values that say what it
-- was. The ordinal is what keeps two captures failing the same way reporting in the
-- same order.

-- Five entries and a request can carry several of them at once. A body naming a
-- source nobody holds is a store failure and a health decision that never ran; a
-- refused envelope is a boundary entry and a source failure both. Nothing here
-- collapses them, because each names a different node and a different thing to go and
-- look at.
failure AS (
  SELECT
    1 AS ordinal,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'node', 'Store Raw Capture',
      'store_error', c.store_error) AS entry
  FROM capture c
  WHERE c.store_error IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    2 AS ordinal,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'node', 'Judge Capture Envelope',
      'contract_version', c.contract_version,
      'capture_faults', c.capture_faults) AS entry
  FROM capture c
  WHERE NOT c.envelope_accepted

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    3 AS ordinal,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'node', 'Extract Capture Records',
      'config_errors', c.config_errors) AS entry
  FROM capture c
  WHERE jsonb_array_length(c.config_errors) > 0

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    4 AS ordinal,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'node', 'Apply Capture Health',
      'source_id', c.source_id,
      'consecutive_failures', c.consecutive_failures,
      'flagged', to_jsonb(c.source_flagged)) AS entry
  FROM capture c
  WHERE c.source_failed

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    5 AS ordinal,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'node', 'Score Capture Findings',
      'error', c.score_error) AS entry
  FROM capture c
  WHERE c.score_error IS NOT NULL
),

-- The three things the insert writes, worked out before it runs so that the statement
-- below is a write and not a decision.
outcome AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN NOT c.document_exists
        THEN 'failed'
      WHEN c.source_failed AND NOT c.document_promoted
        THEN 'failed'
      WHEN c.source_failed OR c.score_error IS NOT NULL
        THEN 'partial'
      ELSE 'ok'
    END AS status,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'captures_received', t.captures_received,
      'sources_read', t.sources_read,
      'sources_failed', t.sources_failed,
      'sources_flagged', t.sources_flagged,
      'envelopes_refused', t.envelopes_refused,
      'records_refused', t.records_refused,
      'documents_written', t.documents_written,
      'documents_promoted', t.documents_promoted,
      'documents_repeated', t.documents_repeated,
      'answers_refused', t.answers_refused,
      'findings_written', t.findings_written) AS counts,
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT jsonb_agg(f.entry ORDER BY f.ordinal, f.entry) FROM failure f),
      '[]'::jsonb) AS entries
  FROM capture c, tally t
),

-- The write. Six columns and no others: id and started_at are the table's own, and
-- there is nothing else on a runs row.

-- domain_id is NULL for a capture that resolved no source, and that NULL is not an
-- empty slot. On runs it means the pass was not scoped to a domain, which is what a
-- maintenance or backfill pass legitimately carries, so a capture nobody could file
-- lands in the same bucket as work that belongs to no domain. Naming a domain anyway
-- is the alternative and there is none to name: the domain is reached THROUGH the
-- source the envelope claimed, and that claim is exactly what failed. The entry in
-- errors is what tells the two apart.

-- status and finished_at are set together because nothing in the schema holds them
-- together. A row saying failed with no finish, or carrying a finish while still
-- saying running, is storable, and runs.status records that only the writer pairs
-- them. Here they are written by one statement and the row is never reopened.
opened AS (
  INSERT INTO runs (domain_id, scheduled_by, status, finished_at, counts, errors)
  SELECT c.domain_id, 'operator', o.status, now(), o.counts, o.entries
  FROM capture c, outcome o
  RETURNING id
)

SELECT
-- The item this node answers, and the last one this workflow emits. Nothing receives
-- it: the webhook answered the request as it landed, and no workflow invoked this
-- one. It is the execution's own record, read by whoever opens the execution
-- afterwards.

-- There is no did-it-land member here, where every other write on this canvas carries
-- one. The insert is unconditional and its RETURNING is read straight out, so a run
-- id IS the answer: the row exists or the statement raised, and there is no third
-- outcome for a member to report.

-- counts and status travel because they are what this node decided, and reading them
-- back off the answer is cheaper than reading the row again.
  (SELECT o.id FROM opened o) AS run_id,
  c.domain_id,
  o.status,
  o.counts,
  jsonb_array_length(o.entries) AS errors_recorded
FROM capture c, outcome o

## Posted, Not Scheduled

This workflow starts when something outside this system POSTs to it, and the Webhook node on this canvas is the whole of what makes that possible. It holds no clock and may not acquire one: `ar-dispatch` carries the only Schedule Trigger in the system, and `tests/invariants/workflows.test.ts` counts them across every built workflow and names the one file allowed to hold one.

It is also the first workflow here that ARMS. `ar-ingest` is reached through an Execute Workflow node, and activating a workflow whose only trigger is that one registers nothing at all; a webhook registers a URL. `scripts/activate-workflows.sh` reads that split off each built artifact rather than off a list kept beside it, which is what lets this file change its answer without an edit anywhere else.

### What arrives, and what has judged it

One item per request, carrying `headers`, `params`, `query` and `body` among others. `body` is the capture envelope, and NOTHING has looked at it: `capture-contract.ts` runs below, after the raw body has been stored, which is the ordering that makes a refused capture a stored failure instead of a lost one. So the first node to read anything off the envelope is `Load Domain Context`, and all it reads is the source the envelope claims.

That read happens in SQL rather than in the expression beside it. The whole body binds as one jsonb parameter, the source id is taken out of it under a bounded digit pattern, and both the pattern and what it refuses are commented at the statement. An expression can import nothing and is read by no gate here, so a rule with any shape to it belongs where a comment can explain it.

### The boundary is the contract, not the caller

What this canvas judges is SHAPE: the envelope against `capture-contract.ts`, and the claimed source id against the `sources` table. Neither of those asks WHO posted, and the Webhook node declares `authentication` as `none`. Arming this workflow therefore publishes a path that writes rows, and whatever fronts the instance is the whole of what stands between that path and anybody who can reach it. `docs/architecture/04-sources.md` is where the contract a client writes to is documented.

## Stored Before Anything Reads It

`Store Raw Capture` writes the request body into `documents.raw` with a `parse_status` of `failed`, and it runs before any node has judged what arrived. The ordering is the whole of this group. It is not a first draft of the write the boundary below would rather make, and it is not a place a pass comes back to.

A push source cannot be re-read. A feed that answered something unusable is fetched again on the next pass, so a refusal there costs one cycle. A capture refused before it was stored is gone, and whoever posted it has already moved on. `src/lib/capture-contract.ts` states the same rule from the other side: every sentence it returns lands in `documents.parse_error` on a row that already exists.

### A later step upgrades the status

Nothing re-runs this write. The group below reads the envelope, and the group after it promotes the row it finds: `parse_status` becomes `ok`, and the `hash`, `url` and `body` the extraction produced are written over the placeholders left here. A refused envelope leaves the row where it is, carrying the boundary's own sentence in `parse_error` and the whole body in `raw` beside it. Two more outcomes sit between those: a source whose `parser_config` could not be read, and a reading of an item this corpus already holds. Each of those updates the account the row gives of itself and leaves the placeholders and the provisional key alone. Every one of them is the same row, moved on rather than written again.

So a row still carrying `failed` and this node's own sentence says something exact: that pass stopped between the store and the boundary. That is the one state this ordering exists to make visible, and it is a row an operator can read, replay against a corrected config, and promote.

### The key is provisional

`documents.hash` is NOT NULL and UNIQUE, and the digest that column eventually carries is over a url and a body neither of which has been extracted yet. So the row is keyed on the posted body under a prefix no content digest can hold, and the promotion replaces it. Recognising a genuine repeat capture is `documents.hash`'s own job and happens there, under the content digest; what the provisional key collapses is a second POST arriving before the first was promoted.

### Two requests have nowhere to be stored

`documents.domain_id` is NOT NULL, so an envelope naming a source this deployment does not hold has no corpus to be written to. A request carrying no body has nothing to store at all. Neither is dropped in silence: the node answers its one item with no document id and a constant sentence saying which, and the groups below refuse the capture on it.
